meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's essay. Why is there a zero on it?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. That's not a crime.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever happens, this stays off his record, and it stays quiet. Is anything on it now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Give me a minute with the scene. Kids misquote; that's a wrong line, not a machine's.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I've read it. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. And you still haven't answered what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. A private rewrite, his mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, Hale, not because he did anything.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put the day and the time in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Mr. Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record, under procedure 4.4. I still require that commitment in writing tonight, including the day and time, and I will confirm with Owen whether Thursday the twelfth works. The rewrite is to be completed before December 1.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight plus Owen's confirmation of the day; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You offered 4.4 in concrete terms (private, after school, mark replaces the zero, nothing on record, in writing) after two pieces of evidence she could check had stood, which met her demand about his record.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history showing a late night on October 28 came close to that night, which is why she answered with a defence and then moved to procedure, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument between an outline and an essay, answer that point directly before moving on, for example by tying it back to the version history times you had already shown.
